To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution of yard sign displays during the 2009 presidential election cycle in Franklin County, OH was spatially clustered at the property level and the Census block level.
the distribution of yard-signs in a neighborhood is influenced by both micro- and meso-social factors, and the micro-social factors have a larger effect than the meso-social factors.

(1) spatial dependence in the distribution of political yard signs exists at both the property and Census block level, (2) spatial dependence is not explained by the traditional predictors of participation (i.e. demographic characteristics of the household), (3) spatial dependence is explained by the spatial distribution of yard sign-displayers in the immediate area, and (4) spatial dependence is partially explained by the spatial location of political yard sign displayers within the Census block.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the micro and macro environments in shaping political participation, and the importance of understanding how political actors use space to influence others.
the spatial patterns of yard sign-display, and we argue that the study is a useful way to understand how the social context shapes the decision to display a yard sign.
understanding why some people are more likely to engage in certain forms of political participation than others.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
yard signs are an effective way to get the message out, but that they are also a way to show your support for a candidate.
the micro- and meso-level contextual effects on yard sign-display are both present and important.
the micro-social environment, interpersonal communication and the meso-social context, and impersonal information all contribute to the decision to display a yard sign.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spatial patterns in the distribution of political yard signs in neighborhoods during elections is the result of both interpersonal and impersonal contextual effects, and that the micro- and meso-level contextual mechanisms interact with one another to create a complex, multi-level spatial pattern of participation.
the spatial distribution of yard signs in neighborhoods is not random.
the spatial pattern of yard sign-display in a neighborhood is the result of a complex interaction between the micro-social and meso-social environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatial dependence in yard sign placement is not a trivial matter.
the study of yard signs provides a unique opportunity for the study of political participation, as it provides a window into the micro and meso social contexts that shape the political landscape.
political participation is not a purely individual-level phenomenon.
